# Creative Control Is Not Economic Control — complete editable platform copy

## 1. LONG VIDEO
Open on a designer and model in one frame. Ask what the picture proves: presence and attribution, not equity, votes, board power, contract term, or sale rights. Move through Ralph Lauren’s public employment agreements, the proxy, and Delaware §141 to build six columns: creative, executive, board, voting, economic, continuity. Close by stress-testing departure.

## 2. SHORT 01
“Final say on the campaign does not necessarily mean final say on the company.” Put CREATIVE APPROVAL and BOARD AUTHORITY on opposite sides, add VOTING POWER, ECONOMICS, and EXIT. End: name the control you mean.

## 3. SHORT 02
“Founder control is not one switch.” Show five sliders—creative, board, vote, money, continuity—at different positions. Voiceover: a title, stock class, employment agreement, and license can each move a different slider.

## 4. CAROUSEL
Cover: SIX CONTROLS HIDING INSIDE “CONTROL.” Then: creative approval; executive authority; board direction; voting power; economics; continuity. Final frames: attach the governing record; run the departure test.

## 5. NEWSLETTER
Subject: You can control the collection and still not control the exit. Explain the public Ralph Lauren records as an example of distinct authority layers, not a universal model. Include the six-column audit and five failure scenarios.

## 6. BOARD PREP
One-page opening statement: “This is not a request for unlimited creative discretion. It is a request to define subject matter, decision threshold, evidence, override, term, and post-departure treatment.” Follow with a table of unresolved counsel questions.

## Claim ledger
- **VERIFIED:** Under Delaware law, a corporation's business and affairs are managed by or under the direction of its board unless the statute or certificate provides otherwise. (S52)
- **VERIFIED:** A public Ralph Lauren employment agreement assigns specified creative-direction authority by contract, while the company's proxy and annual report separately describe voting power, offices, and corporate governance. (S50, S36, S37)
- **INFERENCE:** Creative approval, board authority, voting power, equity economics, and employment status are different control layers. (S50, S52, S37)

## Publication discipline
Use the copy as written with the package's rendered social artwork. Preserve captions, alt text, creator and institution credits, canonical URLs, evidence labels, labor and jurisdiction limits, participant correction, and counsel or specialist boundaries.
